sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant is in jail since 01.08.2022.
He submits that after rejection of the appellant's earlier appeal, though six months have passed, but still charges have not been framed in the trial.
He further submits that if the statement of prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161 and 164 of the CrPC is seen, then it will be clear that it is a case of consent.

He submits that the prosecutrix who is a married lady aged about 32 years, though stated that at the time of incident she shouted, but nobody has come to help her, on the contrary, the story is otherwise as after the incident when she came out from the room and noticed that one person namely Guddu standing outside the room has seen the incident then she has no option but to lodge the complaint.
He submits that in the medical report, no sign of any injury was found over the body of the prosecutrix.
He submits that after shouting by the prosecutrix, it is almost impossible that a person standing outside the room would not come for her help.

According to him, it was a case of consent and only after coming to know about the fact that the incident has been seen by some other person, then only the prosecutrix lodged a false complaint against the appellant.
Therefore, he prays that looking to the aforesaid facts and circumstances of the case and the appellant's custody period,
he may be enlarged on bail.
On the other hand, learned Panel Lawyer has opposed the prayer of bail and submitted that delay cannot be a ground for bail.

He has submitted that the order-sheets of the trial make it clear that the delay is being caused only at the instance of the defence as time and again, instead of arguing the matter on charge, they are taking adjournment.

Learned counsel for the objector has also supported the submissions advanced by learned Panel Lawyer and submitted that it is not a case in which after seeing the incident by a person, report was lodged, but on the contrary, after getting support of that person, the prosecutrix lodged the report on the same day.
He has further submitted that it is not a case of consent whereas it is a case of rape committed by the appellant.
He has submitted that looking to the nature of crime committed by the appellant, this appeal deserves dismissal.

Considering the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties, perusal of case diary, the fact that being an under trial accused the appellant is in jail since 01.08.2022 and the charge is yet to be framed
, I am inclined to enlarge him on bail.

Therefore, without commenting anything on the merits of the case, this appeal is allowed subject to a condition that after release on bail, the appellant will not try to make any contact with the prosecutrix in any manner.

It is made clear that if such an act is reported against the appellant, then the respondent/State will be at liberty to move an appropriate application for cancellation of bail granted to the appellant.

It is directed that the appellant be released on bail upon his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- with one solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Court concerned for his appearance on the dates given by it.
It is further directed that the appellant shall abide by the conditions enumerated in Section 437(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
